subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode & pricing (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Smith <lauren.smith@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 8 Apr 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode & pricing (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Lauren —

Thanks again for the demo and the deep dive today. Quick recap and next steps from my side to make sure we align on deployment mode and initial cost expectations: 

1) Requirements we heard you prioritize:
- High throughput for batch inference (up to ~5M tokens/day)
- Strict data residency & encryption requirements for transaction data
- Desire for predictable monthly spend and SLA for peak business hours

2) Initial recommendation (to validate):
- Primary: Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) to meet throughput + SLA
- Secondary: Private VPC if procurement requires VPC endpoints or on-prem options for sensitive workloads
- Hosted API only for non-sensitive, lower-throughput use cases or pilot workloads

3) Pricing note (high level):
- Hosted API: per-token pricing with predictable unit economics for low volume, but can be more expensive at high sustained throughput
- Dedicated: committed capacity (monthly GPU pool) with discounted unit cost; good if you can commit to baseline throughput
- Private (VPC/on-prem): higher fixed setup + infra costs but lower marginal cost and full control — better if you expect multi-year heavy usage

I attached a quick capacity-costing workbook (Redwood_Capacity_Costing.xlsx) with a few sample scenarios — the tab labeled "FintechCo-proj" models per-token equivalent costs for Hosted vs Dedicated with different commit levels.

Could you confirm: 1) whether you have a procurement timeline (SOW/PO cadence), and 2) whether a Dedicated commitment looks like an option (approx monthly spend range ok) versus needing Private/VPC from day one?

If helpful, I can draft a 1-pager with two committed-capacity options (conservative vs aggressive) and an appendix with a 24-month TCO comparison for Private. Happy to schedule a quick call with Neha to walk through the workbook.

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0139

Attachments: Redwood_Capacity_Costing.xlsx, SOC2-compliance-overview.pdf

From: Lauren Smith <lauren.smith@fintechco.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, FintechCo Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & pricing (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Thanks for the summary, Aditya — super helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Data residency: we need EU residency for production PII processing. That doesn't rule out Dedicated (if hosted in EU region) but Private VPC would be required if the data must never touch public/shared control planes.
- Throughput: peak batches will be heavy (~5M tokens/day) and predictable during month-end processing windows. We want predictable latency during those windows.
- Procurement timeline: we're targeting vendor selection by end of May; procurement and legal will need SOW + security paperwork approved by 6/15.

Could you send a short committed-capacity example (monthly GPU count + price) and an equivalent per-token estimate for Hosted for the projected volumes? Also please include any setup/one-time fees for Private VPC and an estimate of 24-month TCO if we went Private.

Looping in procurement to start the SOW checklist.

—Lauren
Director of Data Engineering | FintechCo
lauren.smith@fintechco.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Smith <lauren.smith@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2026 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & pricing (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Lauren — great context, thanks. Attached workbook updated (tab: FintechCo-proj) and high-level numbers below to help procurement: 

High-level cost examples (ballpark, USD):
- Hosted API (per-token): $0.0008 / token (generation model mix) — for 5M tokens/day -> ~$120/day -> ~$3,600/month.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): 4x A100-equivalent GPUs reserved monthly: ~$28,000/month committed. Effective per-token at projected utilization: ~$0.00025/token (includes autoscaling buffer + support SLA).
- Private VPC / On-prem: one-time setup & infra onboarding estimate: $150k–$250k (depending on network & KMS/HSM integrations) + ongoing infra ops (approx $15k–$25k/month). Over 24 months, breakeven vs Dedicated is plausible if sustained utilization is >85% of reserved capacity.

Notes / assumptions:
- Hosted per-token assumes mixed model usage; higher quality models increase per-token price.
- Dedicated pricing example assumes committed baseline capacity to cover peak windows with autoscale buffer; we can provide tiered commit options (2, 4, 8 GPU pools) with step discounts.
- Private VPC quoted costs are initial estimates; we would engage Engineering to finalize a SOW and network assessment.

Next steps I propose: 
1) I’ll prepare two committed-capacity options (2-GPU, 4-GPU) with exact list prices and expected effective per-token costs.
2) Neha can schedule a 45 min technical call next week to validate latency/SLOs in your EU region and walk procurement through security artifacts (SOC2, data handling).
3) If procurement wants an MSA/SOW template, Marissa can share a cap-ex vs op-ex summary for the Private path.

Can you confirm available times for a tech call next Wed or Thu?

Thanks,
Aditya

From: Lauren Smith <lauren.smith@fintechco.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, FintechCo Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & pricing (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Aditya — appreciate the fast turnaround. Wed (4/14) 10:00–11:00 PT or Thu (4/15) 13:00–14:00 PT both work for the team. Procurement prefers the 4-GPU committed example initially. Please include line items they can reference in the SOW (setup fees, monthly committed, overage rates, EU region notes).

We expect to share initial security questionnaire responses by 4/20. If you can include a rough 24-month TCO comparison in the committed-capacity doc that would be ideal.

Thanks — looking forward to the tech call.

—Lauren
